papers.title: 3D Scene Graphs: Open Challenges and Future Directions
papers.summary: 3D scene graphs (3DSGs) have emerged as a powerful representation for spatial AI by combining geometric grounding with semantic and relational abstractions of the environment. Their expressiveness has made them relevant to a broad range of problems in robotics and computer vision, including manipulation, navigation, task planning, scene understanding, and many others. papers.title: PhantomTac: Hijacking Robotic Tactile Systems with Deploy-and-forget Tags
papers.summary: Tactile perception is crucial for precise robotic manipulation, providing an important foundation for dexterous, closed-loop force control. Among various tactile sensing techniques, magnetic tactile sensors stand out thanks to their fine-grained, three-dimensional force perception capability and strong robustness against visual occlusion. In this study, we discover a physical loophole called PhantomTac in magnetic tactile sensors. papers.title: Coordination without command: active inference and the route to embodied intelligence
papers.summary: Embodied intelligence depends on bodies whose contact with the environment, distribution of load and capacity for action are only partly known and are changed by movement. We argue that this creates a practical reason to organize inference through distributed, hierarchical and plural processes, using active inference to relate local belief updating, contextual constraints and action selection within a common framework. papers.title: Robotic Platforms for Green Vehicle Refueling and Charging Stations: A Critical Review of Fixed, Mobile, Humanoid, and Legged Solutions
papers.summary: Robotic automation of vehicle refueling and charging stations is an emerging enabler of sustainable transportation, but the relevant platforms are studied in disconnected communities. This review compares two evidence-based platform families (fixed and mobile manipulator arms) and two emerging candidates (humanoid and quadruped robots) across EV conductive charging, EV wireless charging with actuated alignment, hydrogen refueling, and battery swapping. papers.title: Reconciling Discrete-Time Mixed Policies and Continuous-Time Relaxed Controls in Reinforcement Learning and Stochastic Control
papers.summary: Abstract. Reinforcement learning (RL) is currently one of the most prominent methods for optimizing dynamical systems, with breakthrough results across various fields. In the RL literature, such problems are typically formulated and solved using mixed policies, from which random actions are sampled at each time step. papers.title: Less Effort, Shorter Proofs: Reinforcement Learning for Security Protocol Analysis in Tamarin
papers.summary: Tools like Tamarin and ProVerif have achieved notable success in analyzing and verifying complex real-world protocols such as EMV, 5G, and WPA2, even detecting zero-day exploits. Despite these successes, verifying such protocols remains a time-consuming, challenging task, often requiring significant human effort and expertise. In this paper, we present a reinforcement learning (RL) framework inspired by AlphaZero and AlphaProof that implements a new style of proof search for Tamarin. papers.title: Imitation-Initialized Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Decision-Making In Settlers of Catan
papers.summary: This paper studies how to train a reinforcement learning agent for Settlers of Catan, a board game that is difficult to learn because of dice randomness, hidden opponent cards, a large action space, and sparse win/loss rewards at the end of a long game. papers.title: GhostTac: Manipulating Tactile Sensors without Physical Contact
papers.summary: Tactile sensors are integral components of modern robotic systems, enabling robots to perceive and interact with the physical environment through tactile feedback. Despite their importance, the physical-layer security of tactile sensors has received little attention in prior work. In this paper, we present GhostTac, to the best of our knowledge, the first contactless attack that manipulates tactile sensing via electromagnetic interference (EMI). papers.summary: This study presents a preliminary geometric modeling workflow for a robotic station planned for an existing production hall. papers.title: Navigated robotic guidance for minimally invasive bertolotti resection technical feasibility and workflow evaluation
papers.summary: Abstract Bertolotti syndrome is characterized by symptomatic lumbosacral transitional vertebral anatomy in which an enlarged transverse process articulates or fuses with the sacrum or ilium. Diagnosis can be difficult because transitional anatomy is common, symptoms may overlap with other spinal disorders, and the pain generator may arise from the pseudoarticulation, adjacent disc or facet, instability, or nerve compression. papers.summary: Global manufacturing industries face profound structural transformations driven by robotic automation, relative factor-price volatility, rising product-market markups, and stringent decarbonization mandates. Although extensive empirical and theoretical literatures have investigated production cost efficiency, profit maximization, and input substitution individually, these research streams remain largely fragmented across industrial organization, macroeconomics, and productivity econometrics. Design and Development of AI-Assisted Wearable Robotics for Healthcare Applications
papers.summary: The rapid advancement of wearable robotic technologies has opened new possibilities for improving healthcare delivery, rehabilitation, and patient mobility. This paper presents the design and development of an AI-assisted wearable robotic system intended to support healthcare applications such as physical rehabilitation, mobility assistance, and injury prevention. The proposed system integrates lightweight wearable hardware with intelligent control algorithms to adaptively assist human motion in real time. papers.title: Reinforcement Learning to Rank Using Coarse-grained Rewards
papers.summary: Learning to rank (LTR) plays a crucial role in various Information Retrieval (IR) tasks. Although supervised LTR methods based on fine-grained relevance labels (e.g., document-level annotations) have achieved significant success, their reliance on costly and potentially biased annotations limits scalability and alignment with realistic goals. In contrast, coarse-grained feedback signals, such as duration time and session-level engagement, are more accessible and affordable. papers.title: Token Buncher : Shielding LLMs from Harmful Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning
papers.summary: As large language models (LLMs) continue to grow in capability, so do the risks of harmful misuse through fine-tuning. While most prior studies assume that attackers rely on supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for such misuse, we systematically demonstrate that reinforcement learning (RL) enables adversaries to more effectively break safety alignment and facilitate more advanced harmful task assistance, under matched computational budgets. papers.title: Scaling medical imaging report generation with multimodal reinforcement learning
papers.summary: Abstract In medical imaging report generation, supervised fine-tuning can overfit to superficial patterns and generalize poorly across institutions. papers.title: Robustness of Vision Language Models Against Split-Image Harmful Input Attacks
papers.summary: Vision–Language Models (VLMs) are now a core part of modern AI. Recent work proposed several visual jailbreak attacks using single/ holistic images. However, contemporary VLMs demonstrate strong robustness against such attacks due to extensive safety alignment through preference optimization, e.g., reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). papers.title: CPPainter: Painting Cell-Penetrating Peptides for Identification and Generation through Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Abstract Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) are promising intracellular delivery vectors, but computational CPP identification, sequence optimization, and candidate generation are often studied as separate tasks. This study aimed to develop an integrated framework for CPP prediction and reward-guided sequence design. We developed CPPainter, a computational framework that couples a protein language model ensemble classifier with a reinforcement-learning-guided generator. papers.title: Algorithm optimization and application overview of multi-agent reinforcement learning
papers.summary: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has gained growing interest for handling distributed decision-making in complex environments. Unlike single-agent settings, MARL involves interacting agents whose policies co-evolve, leading to non-stationarity. This paper reviews the stochastic game formulation for MARL, then classifies existing algorithms into fully centralized, fully decentralized, and centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) paradigms. papers.title: DSS: Dynamic Semantic Steering for Robust Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models
papers.summary: Text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models have introduced new security risks, as adversaries can exploit flexible text prompts to induce the generation of sensitive or policy-violating content (e.g., NSFW or copyrighted concepts). Concept erasure has emerged as a promising defense, aiming to suppress targeted semantics while preserving benign generation. papers.title: Real-time Indian Sign Language word recognition through visual detection and temporal word construction
papers.summary: Indian Sign Language recognition is important for accessible human-computer interaction, yet constrained by limited datasets, signer variability, and difficulty converting frame-level detections into coherent words. This paper presents a framework for real-time finger-spelled Indian Sign Language word recognition from video. Our system focuses on character-level detection and temporal word construction, not continuous sentence-level ISL. papers.title: Automated Identification of Parasitoid Wasps for Biological Control Monitoring Using an Optimized Single-Stage Detector
papers.summary: Parasitoid wasps are important biological control agents, but their small size and subtle morphological differences hinder rapid identification and require taxonomic expertise. This study developed a computer vision framework for recognizing parasitoid wasps from single-plane microscopy images. A dataset of 3420 images representing 36 parasitoid taxa and 38 terminal biological classes was assembled.
